global_issues.title: US-Iran strikes paused for diplomacy as Hormuz talks advance
global_issues.note: Confirmed by CBS News, NPR, Al Jazeera, Japan Times (2026-07-26/27): US and Iran extended pause in strikes for a second/third straight day, Oman mediating talks on reopening Hormuz with fewer transit restrictions. Consistent with briefing.

global_issues.title: US-China semiconductor controls shift to case-by-case licensing
global_issues.note: BIS rule effective 2026-01-15 shifted H200/MI325X-class licensing from presumption-of-denial to case-by-case review; VEU status expired, requiring new annual licenses for TSMC/Samsung/SK Hynix. However this framing is now overshadowed by a much larger and unrelated story: a severe chip-stock selloff on 2026-07-28 driven by Chinese memory competitor CXMT's 466% Shanghai debut and AI-valuation fears, not export-control policy. See missing_major_news.

Briefing states TSM closed at $392.31 with pre-market $394.32 (+0.51%). Independent sources report a prior close near $399.09 and a ~3.61% decline on 2026-07-28 (implying a close nearer ~$384-387), which does not reconcile with the briefing's $392.31 figure or its implied flat/positive pre-market move.

grok_report.summary: The three global macro items (Hormuz, chip export licensing, Taiwan Strait) are each individually accurate but stale or incomplete in framing, and the briefing misses the day's dominant market story — a sharp AI/semiconductor selloff triggered by Chinese memory competitor CXMT's IPO, which better explains the SMH/QQQ downtrend than the cited 'supply chain/rates' rationale. More seriously, five watchlist tickers (MU, AMZN, MSFT, AAPL, CRWD) are erroneously tagged as untracked 'Recent IPOs' despite being long-established stocks, and TSM's quoted price conflicts with independently reported figures — these look like underlying data-pipeline defects rather than narrative judgment calls.
